stemMd: For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 3 mol of H₂ and 1 mol of O₂ react completely as far as possible. How many moles of water form?
explanationMd: One mole of oxygen needs two moles of hydrogen and gives two moles of water. Three moles of hydrogen are available, so oxygen is limiting. The reaction forms two moles of water and leaves one mole of hydrogen unused.

distractorRationale.d: This fails to use the coefficient of two for water.
distractorRationale.e: Hydrogen is in excess; oxygen cannot support three moles of water.
distractorRationale.a: One mole of oxygen produces two, not four, moles of water.
distractorRationale.b: This multiplies reactant quantities without applying the balanced ratio.
